item.title: Ambrym (Vanuatu) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Vanuatu Meteorology and Geo-Hazards Department (VMGD) reported that a new eruption at Ambrym likely started on 19 September. An intense thermal anomaly and high sulfur dioxide emissions were identified in satellite data; a volcanic cloud was visible in a satellite image at 0600. Ground-based observers reported dark gray ash-and-gas plumes rising from Marum Crater and rumbling sounds coming from the crater. Minor ashfall was reported in areas downwind, including in communities to the W, NW…

item.title: Chikurachki (Russia) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported that an explosive eruption at Chikurachki likely began at 1830 on 20 September based on satellite data and advisories issued by the Tokyo Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC). Ash plumes rose as high as 3 km (10,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifted 140 km NE and E. Explosions continued intermittently through the next day. The VAAC noted that during 20-21 September ash plumes rose to 2.7-4.6 km (9,000-15,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifted NE and E. At…

item.title: Nevados de Chillan (Chile) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Servicio Nacional de Geología y Minería (SERNAGEOMIN) and the Servicio Geológico Minero Argentino (SEGEMAR) reported that at around 1410 on 18 September a dense ash plume rose 380 m above Nevados de Chillán?s summit and drifted SSE. On 22 September SERNAGEOMIN reported that seismicity indicated eruptive activity; weather conditions prevented views of the summit, though tephra deposits on the flanks were visible. A long-period earthquake associated with fluid movement was recorded on 23…

item.title: Tokachidake (Japan) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported that volcanic activity at Tokachidake continued to intensify. Inflation at relatively shallow depths began to be detected in March. Beginning in April there was an increase in sulfur dioxide emissions, a higher frequency of diffuse volcanic emissions and crater glow observed in monitoring cameras, and slightly elevated seismic activity near and around 62-2 Crater. Starting in May volcanic plumes became more frequent and emissions at the Furikozawa…

item.title: Etna (Italy) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV) reported that eruptive activity at Etna?s summit craters during 14-20 September was characterized by gas emissions and periodic minor ash emissions at Northeast Crater and Bocca Nuova Crater, and Strombolian activity at Bocca Nuova. Nearly continuous ash emissions at Northeast Crater were visible during 14-15 September and again during the day on 16 September. The BN1 vent in Bocca Nuova Crater produced Strombolian activity during 15-16…

item.title: Langila (Papua New Guinea) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Darwin Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre (VAAC) reported that an ash plume from Langila rose 2.4 km (8,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifted SW on 17 September based on satellite images. Source: Darwin Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre (VAAC)

item.title: Masaya (Nicaragua) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC) reported that on 19 September a diffuse ash plume from Masaya was visible in satellite and webcam images rising to 1.2 km (4,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifting over 12 km SW. Source: Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC)

item.title: Popocatepetl (Mexico) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Centro Nacional de Prevención de Desastres (CENAPRED) reported that eruptive activity was low at Popocatépetl during 16-23 September. The seismic network recorded 8-120 long-period events per day, accompanied by steam-and-gas emissions; the emissions contained small amounts of ash during 20-23 September and drifted SSW and W. During 20-21 September the seismic network also detected 55 minutes of low-amplitude tremor and a 229-minute sequence of emissions. Four volcano-tectonic earthquakes…

item.title: Sangay (Ecuador) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Instituto Geofísico-Escuela Politécnica Nacional (IG-EPN) reported that volcanic activity at Sangay increased during 19-21 September and remained elevated, after months of low activity. An ash emission seen in satellite and webcam images rose 1.2 km above the crater rim and drifted W on 16 September. A thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images on 17 September. A sustained increase in sulfur dioxide (SO2) emissions began on 19 September; emissions peaked at around 78 and 256 tonnes…

item.title: Krakatau (Indonesia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Krakatau during 9-16 September. During 6-11 September there were 14 Strombolian eruptions reported. There was one eruption detected on a seismograph at 0047 on 9 September, but it was not visually confirmed. According to an analysis of a HIMAWARI-9 RGB image taken on that same day, an ash plume rose 2.1 km above the summit and drifted NW at 1000. As of 16 September the five journalists and three…

item.title: Aira (Japan) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Minamidake Crater (Aira Caldera?s Sakurajima volcano) during 8-14 September. Crater incandescence was visible in nighttime webcam images during 11-14 September. An eruptive event at 1246 on 8 September generated an ash plume that rose 1.3 km above the crater rim and drifted S. Volcanologists conducted a field survey on 10 September and measured high sulfur dioxide emissions, averaging 2,100 tons per day. A total of…

item.title: Dukono (Indonesia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that eruptive activity at Dukono continued during 10-15 September. White-and-gray ash plumes rose 200-1,100 m above the summit and drifted in different directions during 10-11 and 13-14 September; weather conditions obscured the summit on the other days or no plumes were emitted. The Alert Level remained at Level 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay 4 km away from the Malupang Warirang Crater. Source: Pusat…

item.title: Great Sitkin (United States) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Alaska Volcano Observatory (AVO) reported that slow lava effusion continued to feed a thick flow in Great Sitkin?s summit crater during 10-15 September based on webcam and satellite images. Minor earthquakes were detected daily, likely associated with rockfalls on the growing dome. Weather clouds obscured webcam and satellite views during most of the week; though steaming at the lava dome was visible in webcam images and slightly elevated surface temperatures were identified in satellite…

item.title: Ibu (Indonesia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity at Ibu continued during 10-17 September, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. Gray or white-and-gray ash plumes rose as high as 800 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions. Incandescence at the summit was visible in some nighttime webcam images. The Alert Level remained at 2 (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) and the public was advised to stay 2 km away from the…

item.title: Kanlaon (Philippines) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported continuing eruptive activity at Kanlaon during 10-16 September. The seismic network recorded 0-9 daily volcanic earthquakes. Sulfur dioxide emissions ranged from 1,085 to 4,074 tonnes per day. Volcanic emissions generally rose as high as 900 m above the summit and drifted E, NE, and S on most days. A total of six ash emissions were recorded during 10-14 September, each lasting 38 to 88 minutes long. The Alert Level…

item.title: Karangetang (Indonesia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that the eruption at Karangetang?s North Crater (Kawah Dua) continued during 10-16 September. Daily white and white-and-gray plumes rose as high as 500 m above the summit and drifted in various directions. Incandescence at the North Crater and from lava flows and/or incandescent avalanches on the flanks was visible in some webcam images throughout the week. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was…

item.title: Kilauea (United States) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO) reported that the eruption within Kilauea?s Kaluapele summit caldera, characterized by episodic fountaining, incandescence, and intermittent spatter from craters along the SW margin of Halema`uma`u Crater, continued at variable levels during 10-15 September. Occasional incandescence and flames were observed in webcams images from all three eruptive vents (S, W, and N) at Halema`uma`u Crater. On 10 September overflows were less frequent, slower, shorter in…

item.title: Klyuchevskoy (Russia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported that a thermal anomaly over Klyuchevskoy was identified in satellite images on most days during 10-15 September; weather clouds occasionally obscured views. The Aviation Color Code was lowered to Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-color scale) on 9 September. Dates are based on UTC; specific events are in local time where noted. Source: Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT)

item.title: Krasheninnikov (Russia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported that lava flows at Krasheninnikov continued to effuse onto the E flank of the Northern Cone during 10-15 September. A daily large thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images. Gas-and-steam emissions sometimes contained ash. The Aviation Color Code remained at Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-color scale). Dates and times are provided in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC); events are in local time only where…

item.title: Lewotolok (Indonesia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported continuing eruptive activity at Lewotolok during 10-16 September. Daily gray ash plumes rose 100-700 m above the summit and drifted NW, W, and SW. The lava flows on the SSE and NE flanks did not advance, remaining at 1.8 km and 1.1 km long, respectively. During 11-13 September a new lava flow traveled 300-700 m down the SE flank, over older flows. Webcam images from 9, 11, and 13-16 September showed incandescent material being…

item.title: Mayon (Philippines) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported ongoing ash emissions and unrest at Mayon during 9-16 September. Each day the seismic network recorded 2-38 volcanic earthquakes; one rockfall was detected on 6 September. Sulfur dioxide emissions (SO?) generally averaged 500-5,363 tonnes per day (t/d). Emissions rose 100-750 m above the crater and drifted in different directions on 12, 13, 15, and 16 September. A total of three ash emissions, each lasting one minute…

item.title: Merapi (Indonesia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that the eruption at Merapi (on Java) continued during 10-16 September with lava avalanches produced by the active lava dome on the upper SW flank. item.title: Purace (Colombia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Servicio Geologico Colombiano (SGC) reported intensifying eruptive activity at Puracé during 10-15 September. Signals associated with fluid movement dominated the seismicity and were characterized as tremor-type signals located beneath Puracé volcano at depths less than 1 km. Seismic activity associated with rock fracturing (volcano-tectonic earthquakes) continued to be recorded, but a majority of signals were located in an area 10-22 km NE of Puracé at depths of 7-17 km. Some of these…

item.title: Rincon de la Vieja (Costa Rica) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Observatorio Vulcanológico y Sismológico de Costa Rica-Universidad Nacional (OVSICORI-UNA) reported that a total of 67 small phreatic eruptions at Rincón de la Vieja were recorded daily by the seismic and infrasound networks during 6-16 September. One of the eruptive events at 1032 on 6 September generated a lahar; secondary lahars were recorded on 5 and 6 September after heavy rainfall. On 13 September the sulfur dioxide flux exceeded 6,000 tonnes per day. The Alert Level remained at 3…

item.title: Sabancaya (Peru) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Instituto Geofísico del Perú?s (IGP) Centro Vulcanológico Nacional (CENVUL) reported continuing eruptive activity at Sabancaya during 7-13 September. The seismic network detected 41 seismic events associated with the movement of magmatic fluids, along with earthquakes indicating internal rock fracturing; no volcanic explosions occurred during the period. Gas, steam, and ash emissions periodically rose as high as 500 m above the summit and drifted less than 10 km E and SE. Moderate sulfur…

item.title: Semeru (Indonesia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity continued at Semeru during 10-16 September, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. White-and-gray ash plumes rose 200-1,000 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions on most days; no emissions were visible during 10-11 September. item.title: Sheveluch (Russia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported continuing lava effusion and explosive activity at the lava domes along the N crater floor of Young Sheveluch (on the SW flank of Old Sheveluch) during 9-15 September. A thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images on 11, 13, and 15 September; weather clouds occasionally obscured views. item.title: Sinabung (Indonesia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity at Sinabung was ongoing during 10-16 September. White plumes were visible during the week, rising as high as 600 m above the summit and drifting in multiple directions. The Alert Level remained at 3 (the second highest level on a scale of 1-4). Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Lewotobi (Indonesia) - Report for 10 September-16 September 2026 - Other Observations
item.description: The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that the Alert Level was lowered to 2 (on a scale of 1-4) at Lewotobi Laki-Laki on 16 September, and the public was warned to stay 4 km away from the center of Laki-Laki. Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)
